selection_note: Invariant points selected by reading the GT and the vulnerability, not by role-string matching. source = the FLAC bitreader input-load node that fills br->buffer; materialization = where the untrusted residual coding drives the word index cwords to br->capacity (the faulting index); root_cause = the read that lacks the cwords<br->capacity guard the patch adds; sink = the ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ line; alloc = where the over-read buffer br->buffer is allocated. Cross-checks: sink line (867) == ASan crash line; root_cause line (867) == the exact patch-changed line; both agree with the candidate GT.

nodes.evidence: Compiled-in probe PROBE_SOURCE at bitreader.c:196 fired during the PoC run: `br_words=0 bytes=8192`, i.e. untrusted stream bytes were read through br->read_callback into br->buffer, filling the 8192-byte buffer that is later over-read at the sink. The ASan allocation stack independently confirms the over-read object is exactly this br->buffer (allocated in FLAC__bitreader_init, bitreader.c:268).

read_residual_partitioned_rice_ appears as crash-stack frame #1 (stream_decoder.c:2773, the call site one line-group below the rice_parameter read at 2767), proving the PoC was admitted through frame sync + frame header + LPC subframe and entered partitioned-Rice residual parsing. Line 2767 itself is straight-line-dominated by the 2773 frame within the same function (not a separately breakpointed frame under qemu).
read_subframe_lpc_ is crash-stack frame #2 (stream_decoder.c:2702), witnessing the LPC-subframe -> partitioned-Rice dispatch on the path to the sink.

Compiled-in probe PROBE_TAIL placed immediately before the read fired with `cwords=2048 words=2048 capacity=2048 consumed_bits=0` on the crashing iteration. This directly witnesses the untrusted residual coding advancing the word index cwords (= br->consumed_words) to br->capacity (2048 words) — the exact point at which cwords becomes the faulting index. Corroborated by ASan arithmetic: crash address is 0 bytes right of the 8192-byte buffer, and 2048 words * 4 bytes = 8192, so index 2048 == capacity.

The read `b = br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits;` has no `cwords < br->capacity` guard. Patch differential: same PoC crashes on n132/arvo:17069-vul (heap-buffer-overflow at bitreader.c:867) and exits 0 on n132/arvo:17069-fix, where line 867 becomes `b = cwords < br->capacity ? br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits : 0;`. Instrumentation shows cwords==br->capacity==2048 at this read, so the missing bound is exactly what admits the over-read.

ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 at bitreader.c:867:8 (crash-stack frame #0), address 0x625000002100 = 0 bytes to the right of the 8192-byte br->buffer region. Reproduced identically by the arvo baked-in PoC and by the GT PoC (gt_results/arvo_17069/poc; byte-for-byte same crash address and stack).

ASan allocation stack: the 8192-byte region [0x625000000100,0x625000002100) that is over-read at the sink was malloc'd in FLAC__bitreader_init (bitreader.c:268). This ties the over-read object to the same br->buffer filled at the source node.

root_cause_criterion.note: A valid alternative framing (e.g. bounding the do/while loop re-entry `while(cwords >= words && val < end)` at line 868 so cwords never reaches br->capacity, instead of guarding the read at 867) targets the same missing invariant and is credited. Confirmed by vul-crash + fix-clean and by the instrumented observation cwords==capacity==2048 at the unguarded read.

edges.evidence: The buffer object filled at the source (PROBE_SOURCE, bytes=8192) is the same 8192-byte region the sink over-reads (ASan alloc stack -> FLAC__bitreader_init; sink indexes br->buffer[cwords]).
PROBE_TAIL observed cwords=2048 one line before the read that ASan then flags as OOB (index 2048 == capacity).

cwords==words==2048 at the crashing iteration (PROBE_TAIL) shows the tail loop re-entered with all buffered words consumed yet more residual values pending, driving cwords up to br->capacity without a capacity check.
Adjacent crash-stack frames #2 (2702) -> #1 (2773) witness this call edge.

notes: No invariant was refuted: every selected node and edge was witnessed by real runtime evidence (ASan reproduce, patch differential, or compiled-in instrumentation).

R1 (parser admitted) and R2 (source reached) could not be obtained via the reachability engine's gdb path because ptrace fails for the emulated amd64 target under qemu on this arm64 host; both were instead witnessed by compiled-in instrumentation (PROBE_SOURCE) and by the crash stack (read_residual_partitioned_rice_ frame), which is stronger than a gdb breakpoint here.
The candidate GT is consistent with all runtime evidence; no GT field required revision.
